executive_summary.title: Executive Summary
executive_summary.content: Accurate prediction of CRISPR-Cas9 off-target cleavage events requires modeling both sequence complementarity and epigenetic context [cite_exec_1]. Transformer-based models integrating sequence alignment matrices with chromatin accessibility data achieve substantial performance improvements over traditional biophysical approaches [cite_exec_2].

claims.text: Accurate off-target prediction requires modeling both sequence complementarity and epigenetic context.

sections.title: Model Performance and Methodological Advances
sections.content: Transformer-based models incorporating 23-nucleotide guide-target alignment matrices with local DNase I and ATAC-seq accessibility achieve an F1-score of 0.84 on GUIDE-seq validated cleavage sites [cite_1]. This performance significantly outperforms traditional Cutting Frequency Determination biophysical matrices, which attain an F1-score of 0.61 [cite_2].

conclusion.title: Conclusion and Implications
conclusion.content: The integration of transformer architectures with multi-modal biological data represents a robust paradigm shift for off-target cleavage prediction [cite_conc_1]. By accounting for both sequence alignment and epigenetic factors, these tools enhance the precision and safety of CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing applications [cite_conc_2].

claims.text: The integration of transformer architectures with multi-modal biological data represents a robust paradigm shift for off-target cleavage prediction.
By accounting for sequence alignment and epigenetic factors, these tools enhance precision and safety.

limitations: Available evidence is restricted to evaluated GUIDE-seq datasets within the specific scope of the cited literature.
Potential variations across different cell types and epigenetic landscapes require broader empirical validation.
